From e4c06479d7059888adf2f22bc1ebcf053bf691a2 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Herbert Xu <herbert@gondor.apana.org.au>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 17:02:45 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] crypto: af_alg - Cap AEAD AD length to 0x80000000

In order to prevent arithmetic overflows when checking the TX
buffer size, cap the associated data length to 0x80000000.

Reported-by: Yiming Qian <yimingqian591@gmail.com>
Fixes: 400c40cf78da ("crypto: algif - add AEAD support")
Signed-off-by: Herbert Xu <herbert@gondor.apana.org.au>

diff --git a/crypto/af_alg.c b/crypto/af_alg.c
index fce0b87c2b65..48c53f488e0f 100644
--- a/crypto/af_alg.c
+++ b/crypto/af_alg.c
@@ -584,6 +584,8 @@ static int af_alg_cmsg_send(struct msghdr *msg, struct af_alg_control *con)
 			if (cmsg->cmsg_len < CMSG_LEN(sizeof(u32)))
 				return -EINVAL;
 			con->aead_assoclen = *(u32 *)CMSG_DATA(cmsg);
+			if (con->aead_assoclen >= 0x80000000u)
+				return -EINVAL;
 			break;
 
 		default:
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary

The patch modifies `crypto/af_alg.c` to add a validation check that caps the AEAD associated data (AD) length to `0x80000000` (i.e., 2^31) in order to prevent arithmetic overflows when computing the TX buffer size.

### Modifications

- **File: `crypto/af_alg.c`**  
  Inside the `af_alg_cmsg_send()` function, after extracting the `aead_assoclen` from the control message, a new check is added:
  ```c
  if (con->aead_assoclen >= 0x80000000u)
      return -EINVAL;
  ```
  This ensures that the association length does not exceed the safe threshold, preventing potential arithmetic overflow in subsequent buffer size calculations.

### Relationship

The change is self-contained within a single function (`af_alg_cmsg_send`) in one file. It does not alter any other parts of the codebase. The fix directly addresses a security vulnerability caused by unchecked large AD lengths.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
con->aead_assoclen = *(u32 *)CMSG_DATA(cmsg);
Reason:
The user-provided AEAD associated data length is directly assigned without any upper bound check. When this value is later used in arithmetic (e.g., adding to other lengths to compute the TX buffer size), a value close to UINT32_MAX can cause an integer overflow, resulting in an undersized buffer that may lead to memory corruption or security issues.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
+			if (con->aead_assoclen >= 0x80000000u)
+				return -EINVAL;
Reason:
The added condition rejects any associated data length equal to or greater than 0x80000000 (i.e., 2^31). This value is less than half of the maximum 32-bit unsigned integer, ensuring that arithmetic operations (e.g., adding to other sizes) cannot overflow because the sum will stay within the range that fits in a signed 32-bit integer, thus preventing the buffer size miscalculation.
